## What the columns are

The parent deck holds the **duration** of each quasi-static ramp segment at 4 ms, so it traverses `vdd_val − 2.0 V` in a fixed time and its supply axis is simultaneously a ramp-rate axis: **242.5 / 325 / 407.5 V/s** at 2.97 / 3.30 / 3.63 V. Every arm below holds one of those two apart from the other, and decomposes each threshold into the three places a moving rail can displace it:

- **V_hys** — the parent deck's own measurand: the rail voltage at the first `POR_RAW = 1.5 V` crossing on each edge, differenced.
- **V_hys at the comparator's own input** — the same pair of rail voltages taken at `SNS = VREF` instead, i.e. where an infinitely fast comparator would decide. The gap between this column and the one before it is everything downstream of the input pair.
- **VREF error** — `bias_core`'s reference at a fixed rail voltage on each edge (2.50 V rising, 2.55 V falling, both clear of every threshold on the ladder), against its own settled value measured on the flat hold of the same run.
- **SNS error** — the sense divider's tap at those same two rail voltages, against the static tap the drawn resistor lengths give (0.461538·VDD with `RHYS` shorted, 0.488563·VDD with it in circuit).
- **comparator+output lag** — the two columns above differenced per edge: how much further the rail travelled between `SNS` crossing `VREF` and `POR_RAW` reaching 1.5 V.

`VREF error` and `SNS error` are the two inputs of the same comparator, so their difference is what the divider ratio refers back out to `VDD`. That makes the decomposition additive and checkable rather than asserted.

One variable: how long each quasi-static segment takes. Supply is pinned at 3.63 V and the corner at `ss`/−40 °C, i.e. exactly the point that fails in the parent record. The 407.5 V/s row **is** the parent deck (`tramp` = 4 ms) and reproduces its 261.092 mV.

| 4 ms | 407.5 V/s | 2.64873 V | 2.38763 V | **261.092 mV** | 236.742 mV | +19.043 mV | -20.756 mV | -1.905 mV | +2.178 mV | +3.739 / +20.611 mV |

| 64 ms | 25.5 V/s | 2.59842 V | 2.44697 V | **151.450 mV** | 145.744 mV | +1.141 mV | -1.317 mV | -0.107 mV | +0.153 mV | -0.100 / +5.806 mV |
| 128 ms | 12.7 V/s | 2.59652 V | 2.44916 V | **147.354 mV** | 142.389 mV | +0.522 mV | -0.696 mV | -0.047 mV | +0.086 mV | -0.078 / +5.043 mV |

`V_hys` falls monotonically with the ramp rate, from 261.092 mV at the parent deck's rate to 147.354 mV at 12.7 V/s. Extrapolating the two slowest rows to a static rail: **V_hys → 143.3 mV**, i.e. mid-window, with a rate coefficient of **0.3216 mV per (V/s)**.

`VREF` is displaced **+19.043 mV** on the up-ramp and **-20.756 mV** on the down-ramp at the parent deck's rate, and the displacement is proportional to the rate (0.04861 mV per (V/s), i.e. 49 µs of equivalent time constant) with an intercept of -0.097 mV — it goes to zero on a static rail. That is not a settling artefact: the same run's own `vref_settled_v` is stable, the displacement reverses sign with the ramp direction, and the down-ramp edge happens several ms after the reference has settled.

The sense divider's tap tracks the rail to within 2.178 mV over the same range — an order of magnitude less than `VREF` moves.

## C — supply swept at ONE ramp rate (242.5 V/s), extracted netlist

One variable: the supply. The parent deck cannot do this — its fixed 4 ms ramp makes rate a function of supply — so this arm stretches `tramp` instead, to hold dVDD/dt at the parent grid's own slowest value. The 2.97 V row is the parent deck's `ss_-40c_2.97v` point unchanged, and reproduces it exactly.

| VDD | ramp | dVDD/dt | VPOR↑ | VPOR↓ | V_hys | parent record's VPOR↑ | parent record's V_hys |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2.97 V | 4.000 ms | 242.5 V/s | **2.62809 V** | 2.41671 V | **211.382 mV** | 2.62809 V | 211.382 mV |
| 3.30 V | 5.361 ms | 242.5 V/s | **2.62809 V** | 2.41243 V | **215.655 mV** | 2.63855 V | 238.555 mV |
| 3.63 V | 6.722 ms | 242.5 V/s | **2.62809 V** | 2.41243 V | **215.655 mV** | 2.64873 V | 261.092 mV |

Rate-matched, the release threshold's spread over the whole ±10 % supply window falls from **20.64 mV** (parent record) to **0.00 mV**, and the hysteresis spread from **49.710 mV** to **4.273 mV**.

**The VPOR↑ column is exactly zero for a reason worth stating plainly, because it is half tautology and half result.** Once dVDD/dt is held constant, all three rows traverse *the same rail trajectory* from 2.0 V up to the crossing — they differ only in where the rail eventually stops, which is after the release has already happened. So of course they agree. The content is the contrapositive: the release threshold depends on the trajectory the rail took to get there and on nothing else, so the 20.64 mV of VPOR↑ spread the parent record attributes to its supply axis cannot be a supply effect — the only thing that differs between its supply columns before the crossing is their rate.

The falling edge does keep a small residual, and it is the down-ramp's own start transient rather than a supply term: at 2.97 V the falling crossing arrives 0.55 V after the rail leaves its hold, against 1.22 V at 3.63 V, so the 2.97 V row has had less of the ramp to develop its steady-state displacement. The 3.30 V and 3.63 V rows, which both have room to develop it, agree to every digit printed.

## D — the decomposition the two parent records could not make

Both parent records measure one rate, so neither can separate hysteresis from displacement. Arms A and B can, by extrapolating each of the three quantities above to a static rail and differencing. At the parent deck's own 407.5 V/s, at the failing corner:

| Term | Schematic | Extracted | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Total measured V_hys** | 248.741 mV | 261.092 mV | **+12.351 mV** |
| Static V_hys (whole path, zero-rate limit) | 143.300 mV | 143.258 mV | -0.042 mV |
| Rate-dependent excess, at the comparator's input (`VREF` displacement × divider ratio) | 97.423 mV | 97.708 mV | +0.285 mV |
| Rate-dependent excess, comparator + output chain | 8.018 mV | 20.126 mV | **+12.108 mV** |

The three lower rows sum to the top one in each column, by construction: the static limit plus the two rate-dependent excesses is the reading.

**The regression the issue reports is the last row.** Of the +12.352 mV the two parent records differ by, **+12.108 mV** is the comparator and its two output inverter stages taking longer to resolve once the extraction's interconnect capacitance is on their internal nodes (`xcmp__VDDA`/`NA`/`CMPO`/`N1`/`TN`/`NBG`: 13.6–21.3 fF each, `layout/postlayout/temp_por_top.spice`). The static hysteresis moves by -0.042 mV and the input-side excess by +0.285 mV — neither is the regression.

**And the reading it regresses is mostly not hysteresis at all.** Of the 261.092 mV the extracted record reports, **55 %** (143.3 mV) is the divider ratio doing its job, **37 %** (97.7 mV) is `bias_core`'s reference being displaced by the moving rail, and **8 %** (20.1 mV) is comparator and output-chain delay. Only the first of the three is the quantity `spec/target-spec.md#por-hysteresis` bounds.

### What this rules out

- **The sense divider's drawn interconnect R/C.** `klt` puts **25.9 fF** on `SNS` and **17.5 fF** on `SNSB` (`C_25`/`C_27`) against a ~5.9 MΩ Thevenin source — ~0.15 µs, three orders below the displacement measured here. The `SNS error` columns confirm it directly: the tap is within 1.90 mV of its static value at the fastest rate on the ladder, against 19.04 mV for `VREF` on the same run.
- **The divider ratio itself.** Its zero-rate hysteresis is 143.3 mV on the extracted netlist and 143.3 mV on the schematic, against a ratified 100 / 150 / 250 mV window — not close to either bound, and within a few mV of the 150 mV typ `design/por_comparator.md`'s sizing algebra targets.
- **A reference that has not settled.** The displacement reverses sign with ramp direction, scales with rate through the origin, and is present on the down-ramp edge several ms after `vref_settle_drift_mv` reads zero.
- **A different reference value.** `vref_settled_v` is 1.19980 V (schematic) and 1.19987 V (extracted) — the two netlists agree on the settled reference to well under a millivolt.
